findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and why it matters, in plain words. This part works.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The only section that could show the promised proof (models, verdict, cost) shows an error instead, and it sits second on the page. A newcomer sees a broken demo before any evidence, which weakens trust in the claims in the opening paragraph.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: A newcomer who came to Athena's site gets a page that is almost entirely about a different project, firstmate. The ledes explain why, but the main body (states, counters, transitions, 45 claims) is about firstmate's internals and does not help them understand or use Athena.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The next step is linked from the top, and the steps give prerequisites, clone, install and a first command. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section: "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link appears in the header but is meant for the repository owner, not a visitor. A newcomer may not know whether it is for them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The study is careful and fully cited, but it is dense and full of jargon (yolo, captain call, places-held, exit 75). Someone new to both projects would struggle to get past the "Start here" section.
findings.source: Transitions, card t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; ..."

findings.text: Saying openly where the source is silent is a real strength for checking the work. But several key words stay undefined, so a newcomer cannot follow every sentence.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "The firstmate source does not define a durable record."

findings.text: The footer sections use Athena's own internal terms (job, recorded boundary, studies/ folder) that are never explained to a visitor.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"
